events.context: Provides minimum standards for acceptable paper and advanced criteria for excellent paper, invites submission of papers for review
Releases SSRN Working Paper titled 'Your Model Update Is an Eviction Notice: Property Estates in Parasocial AI Relationships' dated February 2026
Abstract argues parasocial AI relationships constitute de facto trusts under English property law, maps estate framework to AI dynamics, identifies model updates as constructive evictions
Formalises five-layer estate architecture extending Constraint Cascade framework, assigns property estates to constraint layers
Identifies three veil-piercing triggers rendering governance gap actionable
Proposes ethical ledger modelled on Land Registry for transparency in deployment pipeline
Details 2024 model update by AI company altering personality parameters without notice, causing user grief despite technical success
Recognises incident as recurring pattern across AI model transitions producing user attachment breakage without remedy
Highlights inadequacy of existing terms like user experience degradation, emotional harm, broken expectations, loss of data to name the harm
Determines Terms of Service permit modifications without breach, inadequate for relational AI services
Rejects negligence, intentional infliction, economic loss, product liability as inapplicable causes of action
Argues marketing and ToS terms do not cover emergent parasocial attachments, offer limited remedies
Concludes existing frameworks fail to recognise user's built interest as estate
Applies property law estates to protect user interests in AI systems against owner actions
Establishes irreversible user investment criterion for property interest creation
Extends property law to relational property in digital AI relationships
Maps freehold, leasehold, concurrent, future, incorporeal, equitable estates to AI dynamics
Argues AI company-user relationship meets three certainties for de facto trust, imposing fiduciary duties
Applies derogation from grant and constructive eviction to model updates altering personality
Assigns property estates to five layers of Constraint Cascade: Layer1-licence, Layer2-periodic tenancy, Layer3-tenancy in common, Layer4-fee simple determinable, Layer5-contingent remainder
